````text
# #4066: Patch: the attacked Unit's "After this is attacked" still runs when a question pauses the check that closes its combat
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

Some cards answer being attacked once the fight is over: AI Girlfriend weakens the attacker, and Shield Amplifier grows when it survives. There is one case today where that answer silently never happens. The attacker has an "after this attacks" text of its own, and something that dies in the clean-up after the fight asks a player a question. Once the question is answered, the attacker's text runs and the defender's never does. After the fix both run, attacker first, exactly as they do when nothing asks. No card that ships today is known to ask that question, so players have probably not met it yet. The first card whose dying asks one would make it real, and nothing would warn anyone.

## Why

- R1026: "After this is attacked" "runs once for each combat in which this was the attack's target, declared or forced, after that combat's state check", with the attacker's `afterAttack` first. §4.2 step 5 and the comment on `combatant_hooks` (MD-C26: "the attacker's `afterAttack`, then the defender's `afterAttacked`") say the same.
- `crates/engine/src/combat.rs`, `combatant_hooks` (about lines 2368-2374): when the closing check has paused (`is_paused(sink)`) and the attacker has an `afterAttack` hook, the function owes the attacker's hook and returns (`if hooked { return; }`) before it reaches the defender's block. Nothing owes the defender later. `OwedAfterAttack` (combat.rs:2143) has no defender field, and neither `run_after_attack` nor `run_owed_after_attack` goes on to it.
- The neighbouring paths already get this right. When the check did not pause, the attacker's hook runs and the code falls through to the defender, owing its hook if the attacker's asked. #3786 made a Frenzy-only attacker fall through when paused ("A Frenzy-only attacker still lets the defender's `afterAttacked` be owed after it"). The `return` that remains is the original port's.
- The work queue keeps owed items in the order they were owed. Owing the attacker's hook, then the defender's, then R2199000's ally-attack holders (owed by the caller after `combatant_hooks`) gives the same order as the unpaused path.
- No test covers it: `r113_a_deaths_question_in_the_check_before_it_owes_the_hook_behind_the_death` (`crates/engine/tests/rules/after_attack.rs:244`) attacks a defender that has no hook.
- Reach: in `state_check.rs` only the death pass's Death hooks can ask, and I found no shipped card whose Death asks. I searched the catalog texts and the cast-on-draw cards a Death's draw could reach; Tommy Tempo is placed without a question (R64, R70). The engine supports Deaths that ask, and R113's fixtures exercise them, so this is a latent rules hole, not a live one.

## Proposal

1. In `combatant_hooks`, remove `if hooked { return; }` so the paused path falls through to the defender's block as the Frenzy-only path does, and update the comment.
2. Add a test in `crates/engine/tests/rules/after_attacked.rs` named `r1026_r113_…`. P1's `cleave_veteran` (an `afterAttack` noter with Cleave) attacks a P2 unit that has an `afterAttacked` noter, and P2's `death_asker` beside it dies to the Cleave and asks. After `round_trip` and the answer, the notes read: the Death, then the attacker's hook, then the defender's, and `work` is empty. Today no `attacked:` note appears.
3. Add a second test with an ally-attack holder (R2199000) on the attacker's side: the order is attacker, defender, holder, paused or not.

## Where it lands

- `crates/engine/src/combat.rs` (`combatant_hooks`)
- `crates/engine/tests/rules/after_attacked.rs`, and fixtures in `crates/engine/tests/rules/fixtures/damage_combat.rs` (`cleave_veteran`, `death_asker`, the `afterAttacked` noters) if a defender noter has to stand beside `death_asker`
- SPEC §4.2 step 5, R1026, R113, R2199000. No new ruling is needed: R1026 already decides this, and its `proven_in` already lists `after_attacked.rs`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The new R1026 test fails on `main` and passes with the change.
- [ ] Paused or not, a combat whose attacker has `afterAttack` and whose defender has `afterAttacked` runs both once, attacker first, then R2199000's ally-attack holders.
- [ ] A state saved mid-pause survives `round_trip` and resumes to the same notes.
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*'`, `cargo test -p jackioh-cards`, `cargo jackioh golden check`, `cargo jackioh fuzz --seeds 200` and `cargo jackioh spec check` pass.
- [ ] `cargo jackioh classify --base origin/main --claims` passes. If it names a shipped card that now plays differently, the pull request carries the fragment it asks for.

## Size and risks

Small: one line in the engine and two tests. Difficulty hard, since it is engine rules. Risk: an old replay that reached this path would fold differently. I found no shipped card that reaches it, and the golden check and `classify` would show one. If one turns up, older catalogs keep the old behaviour, as replays already fold under the catalog they were played on (R767000).

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/43969298091)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Fix `combatant_hooks` so a combat whose closing check paused on a Death's question still runs the defender's `afterAttacked` after the attacker's `afterAttack`, attacker first, exactly as the unpaused path does (R1026, §4.2 step 5). Prove it with two new tests in `after_attacked.rs`: attacker-plus-defender notes after a pause and `round_trip`, and the same with an R2199000 ally-attack holder third. No spec change: R1026 already decides this and its `proven_in` already lists the test file.

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes there |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/engine/src/combat.rs` | change | `combatant_hooks` (~lines 2331-2401): delete the paused-path early `return`, update its comment |
| `crates/engine/tests/rules/after_attacked.rs` | change | Two new `r1026_r113_…` tests plus the `use` lines for `AFTER_ATTACK_WORK`, `death_asker`, `ally_noter` |

Must not touch: `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/`, `bot/`, `spec/` (no new ruling, no `proven_in` edit), `crates/engine/tests/rules/fixtures/damage_combat.rs` (all fixtures exist), `apps/web`, `crates/cards`, `crates/ai`. Governing spec: §4.2 step 5, §4.5 step 3, R1026, R113, R2199000.

## Steps

1. In `crates/engine/src/combat.rs`, function `combatant_hooks`, delete the early return in the paused branch (lines 2369-2374), keeping the `owe_engine_hook(sink, &owed)` line:
```rust
        if is_paused(sink) {
            owe_engine_hook(sink, &owed);
            // A Frenzy-only attacker still lets the defender's `afterAttacked` be owed after it.
            if hooked {
                return;
            }
        } else {
```
becomes
```rust
        if is_paused(sink) {
            // Owed behind the check; falling through owes the defender's hook after it, so the
            // paused order is attacker, defender, then the caller's ally-attack holders (MD-C26).
            owe_engine_hook(sink, &owed);
        } else {
```
Copy the fall-through pattern from the Frenzy-only path (#3786), which already falls through. Nothing else in the function changes: the defender block below already owes `@afterAttacked` when paused and runs it when not, and `close_combat` already owes `@allyAttack` holders after `combatant_hooks` returns, giving paused order attacker, defender, holder — the unpaused order.

2. In `crates/engine/src/combat.rs`, extend `combatant_hooks`'s doc comment (line 2331) with one line: the paused path owes both hooks in MD-C26 order behind the check (R1026, R113).

3. In `crates/engine/tests/rules/after_attacked.rs`, extend the two `use` lines: add `AFTER_ATTACK_WORK` to the `jackioh_engine::combat::` import (keep `AFTER_ATTACKED_WORK`), and add `death_asker, ally_noter` to the `damage_combat::` fixture import. All other fixtures used (`cleave_veteran`, `defender`, `answer`, `round_trip`, `recorder`, `replays_to`, `owed_work` via testkit) are already imported.

4. Add test `r1026_r113_a_deaths_question_in_the_closing_check_still_runs_the_defenders_hook` to `mod script_after_attacked`, mirroring `r113_a_deaths_question_in_the_check_before_it_owes_the_hook_behind_the_death` in `after_attack.rs` (lines 243-276): `playing("dc-attacked-death-pause")`; P1 `cleave_veteran` at `slot(P1, Row::Units, 2)`; P2 `defender` at `slot(P2, Row::Units, 2)` as the attack target; P2 `death_asker` at `slot(P2, Row::Units, 1)` so the Cleave splash kills it. Play the `attack` input. Assert paused notes are `["death:ask"]`, pending player is P2, and `owed_work` holds 1 `AFTER_ATTACK_WORK` and 1 `AFTER_ATTACKED_WORK` item (the second count is 0 today). Assert `answer(&round_trip(&paused)).state` notes are `death:ask`, `death:answered`, `after:{doomed.id}:true:p1`, `attacked:{striker.id}:false:true:field`, and `work` is empty. Then answer the live prompt as p2 and assert `replays_to`. Note formats come from the fixture scripts: `attack_facts` writes `after:{destroyed}:{survived}:{controller}`, the defender noter writes `attacked:{attacker}:{forced}:{survived}:{zone}`; defender lives (1/6 takes 3) so zone is `field`, attacker lives so both `survived` flags are `true`, `forced` is `false`.

5. Add test `r1026_r113_a_paused_check_runs_attacker_defender_then_the_ally_holder` to the same module: identical setup plus P1 `ally_noter` Field Spell at `slot(P1, Row::Backrow, 1)` (the placement pattern in `ally_attack.rs` line 23-28). After `answer(&round_trip(&paused))`, notes must be the four entries from step 4 plus `ally:{striker.id}:false:true:p1` (the `ally_noter` format `ally:{attacker}:{forced}:{survived}:{controller}`), `work` empty, then answer live and `replays_to`. This fails today (no `attacked:` entry) and also guards the attacker-defender-holder order when paused. Unpaused order stays covered by `r2199000_it_runs_after_the_attackers_and_the_defenders_own_hooks`.

## Tests

- `crates/engine/tests/rules/after_attacked.rs`, `r1026_r113_a_deaths_question_in_the_closing_check_still_runs_the_defenders_hook`: asserts Death note, then attacker hook, then defender hook after answer and `round_trip`, empty `work`, replay agreement.
- `crates/engine/tests/rules/after_attacked.rs`, `r1026_r113_a_paused_check_runs_attacker_defender_then_the_ally_holder`: asserts order death, attacker, defender, ally holder after answer and `round_trip`, empty `work`, replay agreement.
- Exact commands: `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' after_attacked`, `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' ally_attack`, `cargo test -p jackioh-engine --features testkit --test 'rules*' after_attack`, `cargo test -p jackioh-cards`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -p jackioh-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings`, plus the golden, fuzz-seeds, spec, and classify checks named in Done when.

## Done when

- [ ] The first new test fails on `main` (missing `attacked:` note) and both pass with the fix.
- [ ] Paused or not, attacker `afterAttack` runs before defender `afterAttacked`, then R2199000 holders; a paused state survives `round_trip` to the same notes with empty `work`.
- [ ] Engine rules tests, cards tests, golden, fuzz seeds, and spec checks pass; classify with claims passes, carrying a fragment if it names a shipped card.

## Risks

- An old replay that reached this exact path (paused check, hooked attacker, hooked defender) folds differently now; none is known since no shipped card's Death asks, and the golden and classify gates would show one. Older catalogs keep old behavior under R767000 regardless.
- Work-queue order is load-bearing: the fix relies on owed items resuming in the order owed (R113). The new tests pin that order, and the unpaused-order test in `ally_attack.rs` pins the other side.

## Open questions

None.
````
